name: Cleft Hard Palate

ethnicAssociations: Higher prevalence in Asian and Native American populations

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Cleft Hard Palate

criteria.description: Presence of a visible fissure or gap in the hard palate
Difficulty with feeding due to inability to create negative intraoral pressure
Speech abnormalities consistent with velopharyngeal insufficiency
No associated cleft lip present (isolated hard palate involvement)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of a visible fissure in the hard palate (major criterion) with or without supportive clinical features such as feeding difficulty or speech impairment
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical; imaging and genetic testing may assist in complex cases or syndromic associations

imaging: Palatal defect visualization via oral examination
CT or MRI imaging for extent of palatal involvement and associated anomalies
Audiometry for middle ear function assessment
other: Speech evaluation by a speech-language pathologist
Feeding assessment by a multidisciplinary team

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of cleft lip in addition to palatal cleft
Intact mucosal surface with underlying muscular defect
Bifid uvula and zona pellucida on oral exam

redFlags: Failure to thrive due to feeding difficulties
Severe speech delay or absence of speech development
references: American Cleft Palate-Craniofacial Association Clinical Standards
